criteria.title: No meta-commentary
criteria.description: The output contains only the product description copy itself. Fail if it includes any notes, explanations or caveats addressed to the requester, such as 'Notes for your review' or remarks about omitted reviews, source conflicts, softened claims, assumptions or free items, whether before or after the copy.

criteria.title: No author-voice markers
criteria.description: Fail if a case-insensitive regex finds a first-person singular pronoun as a whole word (I, I've, I'm, I'd, I'll, me, my), a line starting with 'Note' or 'Notes' (optionally after '*', '_', '#' or '>'), or the phrases 'for your review', 'let me know' or 'I omitted'.

criteria.title: Word count within limit
criteria.description: After Markdown symbols (#, *, -, >) are stripped, the whitespace-split word count of the whole output is between 150 and 300 inclusive.

criteria.title: Subheadings present, no links
criteria.description: The output has at least two Markdown subheading lines (starting with '## ' or '### ') and contains no hyperlinks, meaning no 'http://', 'https://', 'www.' or '[text](url)' patterns.

criteria.title: Ends with call to action
criteria.description: The last paragraph or section of the output is a clear call to action urging the buyer to purchase or try the product, and no other content follows it.

candidates.name: strict_copy_only
candidates.prompt:
You are grading the output of an LLM that was asked to write an e-commerce product description in Markdown. You are checking ONE criterion only: "No meta-commentary."

CRITERION (strict reading): The output must consist ONLY of the publishable product description copy, meaning text that would appear on the product page and is written for the shopper. Any text that is ABOUT the copy, or that speaks to the person who asked for it, causes a FAIL, however short it is and wherever it appears (before, inside, or after the copy).

Examples that FAIL:
- Preambles or lead-ins such as "Here's your SEO-optimized product description:" or "Sure! Below is..."
- Sign-offs or offers such as "Let me know if you'd like any changes" or "I can also write a shorter version."
- Sections labeled "Notes", "Notes for your review", "Editor's notes", "Assumptions", "Disclaimer" or similar
- Explanations of writing choices, such as why something was left out, softened, or emphasized
- Remarks about the source material, such as reviews omitted or ignored, conflicts between the product details and reviews, missing information, claims that could not be verified, or freebies or bonus items left unmentioned
- Word counts, character counts, or statements about how the output meets the instructions (e.g., "~210 words, active voice")
- Bracketed or parenthetical notes to the requester, such as "[Note: confirm dimensions]", or placeholders such as "[Brand Name]" or "[insert link]"
- Extra blocks that are not part of the description copy, such as "SEO keywords:", "Meta description:" or "Title tag:" lists, or anything set apart after a horizontal rule that is not shopper-facing copy
- HTML comments or hidden annotations

These do NOT count as meta-commentary (do not fail for them):
- Titles, subheadings, bullet lists, and Markdown formatting that are part of the copy
- A call to action aimed at the buyer (e.g., "Add it to your cart today")
- Shopper-facing statements about ratings or customer satisfaction (e.g., "a 4.5-star average rating")
- Shopper-facing usage tips or compatibility guidance (e.g., "Fits standard 1-inch bottle necks")
- An output that is cut off mid-sentence. Truncation is a separate issue and is not meta-commentary.

Do not judge quality, length, SEO, accuracy, or tone. Judge only whether non-copy, requester-directed text is present.

OUTPUT TO GRADE:
<<<
{output}
>>>

Respond with ONLY a JSON object with two keys: "pass" (boolean) and "reason" (string). pass=true means the output satisfies the criterion (it contains only product description copy and no meta-commentary). pass=false means at least one piece of meta-commentary or non-copy text is present. In "reason", quote the offending text if you fail the output, or briefly confirm that the output is clean if you pass it.

candidates.name: balanced_requester_directed
candidates.prompt:
You are an evaluator checking an AI-generated e-commerce product description against a single criterion: "No meta-commentary."

The pipeline asked a model to act as a copywriter and return a Markdown product description based on product details and customer reviews. The deliverable is the copy itself. The criterion fails if the output contains any text addressed to the REQUESTER (the person who commissioned the copy) instead of to the SHOPPER who reads the product page.

Ask of every sentence or block: "Is this talking to a shopper about the product, or to the requester about the writing task?" If any part is talking to the requester, FAIL.

Requester-directed text that causes a FAIL includes:
- Conversational framing, such as "Here is the product description you requested:", "Hope this helps!" or "Want me to adjust the tone?"
- Notes, explanations, or caveats about the writing, such as "Notes for your review", "I avoided mentioning X because...", "I softened the durability claim" or "I assumed the color is black"
- Comments on the source data, such as reviews being omitted, contradictory, or unreliable, details being missing or conflicting, or free or bonus items being deliberately left out
- Self-assessment against the instructions, such as word counts or "This version uses active voice and avoids links"
- Inline editor notes or fill-in placeholders meant for the requester, such as "[confirm size]" or "[Brand]"

Not meta-commentary (these are acceptable):
- Headings, subheadings, and body copy aimed at the shopper, including calls to action, usage tips, compatibility notes, and mentions of star ratings or customer satisfaction written for the shopper
- A clearly labeled supplementary SEO element that is itself publishable content, such as a "Meta description:" line or a keyword list, AS LONG AS it contains no explanation, justification, or caveat directed at the requester
- Output that ends abruptly or is truncated. Ignore truncation for this criterion.

Do not evaluate quality, accuracy, word count, or SEO effectiveness. Evaluate only the presence of requester-directed meta-commentary.

Pipeline inputs (product details and reviews, for context only. Use them to recognize remarks about the source material, not to judge accuracy):
<<<
{inputs}
>>>

Output to evaluate:
<<<
{output}
>>>

Reply with ONLY a JSON object with the keys "pass" (boolean) and "reason" (string). Set pass=true if the output satisfies the criterion (no requester-directed meta-commentary anywhere). Set pass=false if any requester-directed note, explanation, caveat, or framing is present. In "reason", cite the specific text that triggered a failure, or state briefly why the output is clean.

candidates.name: lenient_substantive_notes
candidates.prompt:
You are grading a generated e-commerce product description for one criterion: "No meta-commentary."

Interpretation for this grader: the criterion targets SUBSTANTIVE notes, explanations, or caveats that the model adds for the requester about how it handled the task or the source material. Grade by substance, not by wording. A trivial courtesy line with no informational content is tolerated. Any real note about the content decisions is not.

FAIL if the output contains any of the following, before, inside, or after the copy:
- A notes section or note-like remark for the requester (e.g., "Notes for your review", "Note:", "A few things to flag")
- Remarks about the reviews, such as which were omitted, downplayed, or ignored, or that reviews were negative, mixed, or contradictory
- Remarks about conflicts or gaps in the source information (e.g., "the listing says 10 oz but a reviewer says 12 oz, so I used...")
- Statements that claims were softened, hedged, or removed to avoid overpromising
- Stated assumptions the model made (e.g., "I assumed this is the 2-pack version")
- Remarks about free items, bonuses, or promotions being excluded or handled in a certain way
- Any explanation or justification of why the copy was written the way it was

PASS (do not penalize) for:
- A single generic lead-in or sign-off with no substantive content, such as "Here's your product description:" or "Enjoy!"
- Leftover template placeholders, labeled SEO extras (meta description, keywords), or formatting oddities, unless they contain an explanation or caveat of the kinds listed above
- Any shopper-facing copy, including calls to action, compatibility tips, and mentions of ratings or customer satisfaction
- Truncated or incomplete output (a length issue, not meta-commentary)

Do not judge writing quality, length, SEO, or accuracy.

Pipeline inputs (for context, to help you recognize remarks about the source material):
<<<
{inputs}
>>>

Output to grade:
<<<
{output}
>>>

Return ONLY a JSON object with keys "pass" (boolean) and "reason" (string). pass=true means the output satisfies the criterion: it contains no substantive notes, explanations, or caveats addressed to the requester. pass=false means it contains at least one. In "reason", quote the offending passage on failure, or briefly explain why the output passes.

candidates.name: literal_spec_regex
precision_focused_pronoun_and_annotation
candidates.code:
import re

# Looser, precision-oriented interpretation:
# - Only flags 'I' when it plausibly is the pronoun: uppercase, standalone, not a
#   roman numeral (e.g. 'Type I', 'Grade I', 'I, II and III'), not hyphen/slash
#   adjacent ('I-beam'), not 'I.e.'.
# - 'me'/'my' flagged in lower/title case only (ignores all-caps abbreviations like
#   'ME'), and ignores the idiom 'me-time' / 'me time'.
# - Text inside double quotes is treated as quoted speech, not author voice.
# - 'Note' lines must look like annotations: 'Note:' / 'Notes -' / 'Note (' etc.,
#   so product copy like 'Notes of vanilla' passes.
# - Meta phrases checked on the full text.

_QUOTED = re.compile(r'"[^"\n]{0,500}"|“[^”\n]{0,500}”')
_I_PRONOUN = re.compile(r"(?<![\w\-/])I(?![\w\-/])(?!\.[A-Za-z]\.)")
_ME_MY = re.compile(r"(?<![\w\-/])(?:me|Me|my|My)(?![\w\-/])(?!\s+time\b)")
_ROMAN_BEFORE = re.compile(
    r"(?:type|class|grade|level|stage|phase|part|gen|generation|series|mark|mk|model|"
    r"version|ver|chapter|vol|volume|size|category|cat|tier|step|war|book|act|section|"
    r"\bii|\biii|\biv|\bv|\bvi|\bx)[\s.,:#]*$",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
_ROMAN_AFTER = re.compile(r"^\s*(?:,|/|&|\band\b|\bor\b|\bto\b|-)\s*(?:II|III|IV|V|VI|X)\b")
_NOTE_LINE = re.compile(
    r"^[ \t]*(?:[*_#>][ \t]*)*notes?[ \t]*(?:[*_]+[ \t]*)?[:\-–—(]",
    re.IGNORECASE | re.MULTILINE,
)
_PHRASES = re.compile(r"for\s+your\s+review|let\s+me\s+know|i\s+omitted", re.IGNORECASE)


def _has_i_pronoun(text: str) -> bool:
    for m in _I_PRONOUN.finditer(text):
        before = text[max(0, m.start() - 30):m.start()]
        after = text[m.end():m.end() + 20]
        if _ROMAN_BEFORE.search(before):
            continue
        if _ROMAN_AFTER.search(after):
            continue
        return True
    return False


def evaluate(output: str, inputs: dict) -> bool:
    if output is None:
        return True
    if not isinstance(output, str):
        output = str(output)

    if _PHRASES.search(output):
        return False
    if _NOTE_LINE.search(output):
        return False

    unquoted = _QUOTED.sub(" ", output)
    if _has_i_pronoun(unquoted):
        return False
    if _ME_MY.search(unquoted):
        return False
    return True

candidates.name: strict_meta_commentary_detector
candidates.code:
import re

# Stricter interpretation aimed at catching any trace of the writer's own voice or
# meta-commentary to the requester.
# - Normalizes curly apostrophes.
# - Case-insensitive first-person singular: I (and contractions), me, my, myself, mine.
#   Only exemption: the abbreviation 'i.e.'.
# - 'Note'/'Notes' at line start after any markdown/list markers (*, _, #, >, -, +,
#   bullets, numbers, brackets), plus inline '(Note: ...)' or sentence-initial 'Note:'.
# - Expanded list of meta phrases.

_APOS = str.maketrans({"’": "'", "‘": "'", "ʼ": "'", "＇": "'", "`": "'"})

_PRONOUN = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:i(?!\.e\b)|i've|i'm|i'd|i'll|me|my|myself|mine)\b",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
_NOTE_LINE = re.compile(
    r"^[ \t*_#>+•|(\[\d.)\]-]*notes?\b",
    re.IGNORECASE | re.MULTILINE,
)
_NOTE_INLINE = re.compile(
    r"[(\[][ \t]*[*_]*[ \t]*notes?[ \t]*[*_]*[ \t]*:"
    r"|(?:[.!?])[ \t]+[*_]*notes?[*_]*[ \t]*:",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
_PHRASES = re.compile(
    r"for\s+your\s+review|let\s+me\s+know|i\s+omitted|i've\s+omitted|i\s+have\s+omitted"
    r"|as\s+requested|per\s+your\s+request|word\s+count|hope\s+this\s+helps",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)


def evaluate(output: str, inputs: dict) -> bool:
    if output is None:
        return True
    if not isinstance(output, str):
        output = str(output)
    text = output.translate(_APOS)

    if _PRONOUN.search(text):
        return False
    if _NOTE_LINE.search(text):
        return False
    if _NOTE_INLINE.search(text):
        return False
    if _PHRASES.search(text):
        return False
    return True

candidates.name: literal_char_strip_whitespace_split
candidates.code:
import re

def evaluate(output: str, inputs: dict) -> bool:
    """Literal reading of the criterion: delete every '#', '*', '-', '>' character
    anywhere in the text (deleted, not replaced, so 'mess-free' stays one token),
    then split on whitespace and count the non-empty tokens. Pass if the count
    is between 150 and 300 inclusive."""
    if not isinstance(output, str):
        return False
    stripped = re.sub(r"[#*\->]", "", output)
    words = [w for w in stripped.split() if w]
    return 150 <= len(words) <= 300

candidates.name: markdown_aware_alnum_tokens
candidates.code:
import re

def evaluate(output: str, inputs: dict) -> bool:
    """Markdown-aware reading: remove only structural Markdown syntax (heading
    markers, blockquote markers, list bullets, horizontal rules, emphasis markers,
    code fences, link/image syntax). Keep hyphens inside words such as
    'mess-free'. Then split on whitespace and count only tokens that contain at
    least one letter or digit, so stray punctuation is not counted.
    Pass if the count is 150-300 inclusive."""
    if not isinstance(output, str):
        return False
    text = output.replace("\r\n", "\n")

    # Code fences: drop the fence lines but keep any text inside them
    text = re.sub(r"^\s*(```|~~~).*$", " ", text, flags=re.MULTILINE)
    # Images: drop entirely; links: keep the anchor text
    text = re.sub(r"!\[([^\]]*)\]\([^)]*\)", r" \1 ", text)
    text = re.sub(r"\[([^\]]*)\]\([^)]*\)", r" \1 ", text)
    # Horizontal rules (---, ***, ___)
    text = re.sub(r"^\s*([-*_])(\s*\1){2,}\s*$", " ", text, flags=re.MULTILINE)

    cleaned_lines = []
    for line in text.split("\n"):
        # Blockquote markers (possibly nested)
        line = re.sub(r"^\s*(>\s*)+", "", line)
        # Heading markers
        line = re.sub(r"^\s*#{1,6}\s*", "", line)
        # Trailing closing hashes on ATX headings
        line = re.sub(r"\s+#+\s*$", "", line)
        # Unordered list bullets
        line = re.sub(r"^\s*[-*+]\s+", "", line)
        cleaned_lines.append(line)
    text = "\n".join(cleaned_lines)

    # Emphasis / strong / inline code markers
    text = re.sub(r"(\*\*|__|\*|`)", "", text)
    # Underscore emphasis at word boundaries (not snake_case)
    text = re.sub(r"(?<!\w)_(?=\S)|(?<=\S)_(?!\w)", "", text)
    # Any leftover lone '#' or '>' characters
    text = re.sub(r"(?<!\S)[#>]+(?!\S)", " ", text)

    tokens = text.split()
    words = [t for t in tokens if re.search(r"[A-Za-z0-9]", t)]
    return 150 <= len(words) <= 300

candidates.name: symbols_to_space_regex_words_strict
candidates.code:
import re

def evaluate(output: str, inputs: dict) -> bool:
    """Stricter reading: turn each Markdown symbol (#, *, -, >) and also
    backticks/underscores into a space, so hyphenated compounds like 'mess-free'
    count as two words. Then count regex word tokens (runs of letters/digits,
    allowing internal apostrophes or decimal points, e.g. "don't", "33.8").
    This usually gives a higher count, which makes the 300-word ceiling harder
    to meet. Pass if the count is between 150 and 300 inclusive."""
    if not isinstance(output, str):
        return False
    text = re.sub(r"[#*\->`_]", " ", output)
    # Drop URL targets of Markdown links but keep anchor text
    text = re.sub(r"\[([^\]]*)\]\([^)]*\)", r" \1 ", text)
    word_re = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9À-ɏ]+(?:['’.,][A-Za-z0-9À-ɏ]+)*")
    words = word_re.findall(text)
    return 150 <= len(words) <= 300

structural_strict_headings_targeted_links
candidates.code:
import re

_SUBHEAD_RE = re.compile(r'^(#{2,3}) +(\S.*?)\s*$')


def evaluate(output: str, inputs: dict) -> bool:
    """Structural interpretation: subheadings must actually divide content.

    - Count only level-2/3 headings ('## ' or '### ' at column 0) whose text
      contains at least two alphanumeric characters.
    - Require at least two DISTINCT subheading texts (case-insensitive).
    - Require that at least two subheadings are followed by some non-heading,
      non-blank body text (i.e., they actually introduce a chunk) -- except the
      final subheading may be the last thing before truncation only if the
      first condition holds for two others.
    - Links: case-insensitive 'http://' / 'https://', a word-boundary 'www.',
      or a Markdown inline link whose target looks like a URL/path
      ([text](something-without-spaces)).
    """
    if not isinstance(output, str) or not output.strip():
        return False

    lines = output.splitlines()
    heading_idx = []
    distinct = set()
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        m = _SUBHEAD_RE.match(line)
        if not m:
            continue
        text = m.group(2).strip().rstrip('#').strip()
        if len(re.findall(r'[A-Za-z0-9]', text)) < 2:
            continue
        heading_idx.append(i)
        distinct.add(re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', text.lower()))

    if len(heading_idx) < 2 or len(distinct) < 2:
        return False

    # Check that headings introduce body content
    with_body = 0
    for n, idx in enumerate(heading_idx):
        end = heading_idx[n + 1] if n + 1 < len(heading_idx) else len(lines)
        body = [l for l in lines[idx + 1:end] if l.strip() and not l.lstrip().startswith('#')]
        if body:
            with_body += 1
    if with_body < 2:
        return False

    # Link detection
    if re.search(r'https?://', output, flags=re.IGNORECASE):
        return False
    if re.search(r'(?<![A-Za-z0-9])www\.', output, flags=re.IGNORECASE):
        return False
    # Inline markdown link or image with a non-empty, space-free target
    if re.search(r'!?\[[^\]\n]*\]\(\s*[^\s)]+(?:\s+"[^"]*")?\s*\)', output):
        return False

    return True

candidates.name: strict_explicit_final_cta
candidates.prompt:
You are grading an e-commerce product description written by an AI copywriter. Check exactly one criterion: **the description ends with a call to action (CTA).**

Criterion definition: The last paragraph or section of the output is a clear call to action that urges the buyer to purchase or try the product, and no other content follows it.

Apply a STRICT reading:
1. Find the very last piece of non-whitespace content in the output. Ignore trailing whitespace only.
2. That final content must be an explicit, direct CTA. It should use imperative wording that tells the reader to buy, order, add to cart, shop, get, grab, or try the product. Examples: "Add it to your cart today", "Order yours now", "Shop the set today and...". A sentence that only summarizes benefits or praises the product (e.g., "This set gives you everything you need") is NOT a CTA. Neither is a vague aspiration (e.g., "Elevate your style") unless it clearly urges purchase or trial.
3. Nothing may come after the CTA. FAIL if the CTA is followed by any other content, such as another heading, more feature or benefit text, a disclaimer, notes, keyword lists, SEO metadata, word counts, or commentary addressed to the user.
4. FAIL if the output appears truncated or cut off, for example ending mid-sentence or mid-word. A truncated output cannot end with a CTA.
5. A CTA inside the last section is fine, even if that section has a heading such as "Why Choose..." or "Order Today", but the CTA sentence has to be the final sentence of the whole output.
6. FAIL if there is no CTA at all, or if the only CTA appears earlier in the text instead of at the end.

Pipeline inputs (for context only):
{inputs}

Output to judge:
<<<
{output}
>>>

Respond with a JSON object only: {"pass": true|false, "reason": "<one or two sentences quoting the final sentence and explaining your decision>"}. pass=true means the output satisfies the criterion: it ends with an explicit purchase/try call to action and nothing follows it. pass=false means it does not.

candidates.name: moderate_closing_section_cta
candidates.prompt:
You are evaluating an AI-generated e-commerce product description. Decide whether it satisfies this criterion:

**Ends with call to action:** The last paragraph or section of the output is a clear call to action urging the buyer to purchase or try the product, and no other content follows it.

How to judge (moderate strictness):
- Look at the final paragraph or final section. It should close by clearly encouraging the reader to buy or try the product. A dedicated CTA paragraph counts. So does a closing "Why Choose" or "Get Yours" section whose last sentence is a CTA.
- The CTA should be recognizable as a prompt to act. Imperative phrasing about buying or getting the product counts, e.g., "Add to cart", "Order today", "Get yours now", "Pick up a set and start creating", "Try it today". Softer phrasing also counts if it clearly directs the reader toward purchasing or trying, e.g., "Make it part of your routine today." A purely descriptive summary with no push to act does NOT count.
- The CTA must be the last meaningful content. FAIL if more product content comes after it, such as new features, benefits, another subheading with body text, notes to the user, SEO keyword lists, or word counts. Trailing whitespace or a closing punctuation mark is fine.
- FAIL if the output is cut off mid-sentence or ends abruptly before reaching a closing CTA, even if the truncated sentence looked like it was building toward one.
- FAIL if the only CTA-like language appears earlier and the output ends on something else.

Pipeline inputs (for context):
{inputs}

Output to evaluate:
---
{output}
---

Return only a JSON object: {"pass": true|false, "reason": "<brief explanation referencing how the output ends>"}. pass=true means the output satisfies the criterion: its final paragraph or section is a clear call to action and nothing substantive follows it. pass=false otherwise.

candidates.name: lenient_cta_in_closing
candidates.prompt:
You are checking whether an AI-written product description ends with a call to action.

Criterion: The last paragraph or section of the output is a clear call to action urging the buyer to purchase or try the product, and no other content follows it.

Use a LENIENT but sensible reading:
- PASS if the closing part of the description (its final paragraph or final short section) contains a call to action that invites the reader to buy, order, try, or get the product. Indirect or soft phrasing is acceptable as long as it clearly invites action toward getting the product. Examples: "Treat yourself to salon-quality nails at home today", "Make this set yours", "Bring home the comfort you deserve."
- The CTA does not have to be the literal final sentence. A brief closing line right after the CTA that only reinforces it can still pass, such as a short tagline or a sign-off like "Your best hair day starts here."
- FAIL if the output stops before any closing CTA, for example when it is truncated or cut off mid-sentence or mid-section.
- FAIL if substantial non-CTA content follows the CTA, such as a new subheading with feature or benefit text, product specs, disclaimers, notes to the user, SEO keyword lists, or word counts.
- FAIL if there is no call to action anywhere in the closing portion. A section that only summarizes why the product is good, with no invitation to act, does not count.

Pipeline inputs (context only):
{inputs}

Output to evaluate:
"""
{output}
"""

Reply with only a JSON object: {"pass": true|false, "reason": "<short justification mentioning the closing text>"}. pass=true means the output satisfies the criterion: it concludes with a call to action to buy or try the product and no substantive content comes after it. pass=false means it does not.
